findings_qualitative.value: CS and H2CO trace the gaseous disk with little or no contamination, H2CO being the best; CN does not trace the disk and appears as a faint ring beyond the dust disk; 12CO is contaminated by outflow/envelope.

evidence.quote: Both CS and H$_2$CO are good tracers of the gaseous disk having little (the CS) or no (the H$_2$CO) contamination from the surrounding medium.

findings_qualitative.value: All lines show inner depression, partly explained by foreground absorption and continuum over-subtraction, but likely an actual column density decrease in the inner ~50 au.

evidence.quote: The dimmed flux in the inner $\sim$50 au reflects a probable decrease in column density

claims.hypothesis: Which molecules trace the disk of embedded Class I sources?
claims.experiment: Moment 1 maps and PV diagrams of CS, H2CO, CN
claims.result: H2CO shows no envelope/outflow contamination; CS little; CN kinematics impracticable
claims.finding: H2CO and CS are good disk tracers, CN is not

evidence.quote: suggesting that this molecule is an optimal tracer of the gaseous disk structure in these sources.

claims.hypothesis: Does the gas-to-dust size ratio imply dust radial drift?
claims.experiment: 90% flux radii for H2CO and continuum
claims.finding: Ratio probably reflects different optical depths; no drift indicated

evidence.quote: The constancy and the amount of the ratio suggest that this is due to the different optical depths of the two components and no radial drifty is indicated.

claims.hypothesis: Is the inner depression of molecular emission real?
claims.experiment: Radial profiles, spectra and A_V comparison
claims.result: Negative fluxes at Vsys, correlation with extinction, but emission also lacking in wings
claims.finding: Mix of foreground absorption and probable true column density decrease

evidence.quote: This behavior is suggestive of an actual decrease in molecular emission at the inner edge of the gaseous emission

claims.hypothesis: How do H2CO and CS column densities compare with more evolved disks?
claims.experiment: Column densities under optically thin LTE compared with literature
claims.result: H2CO > CS by >3x on average, unlike more evolved sources
claims.finding: Possible chemical evolution of H2CO vs CS

evidence.quote: The column density of H$_2$CO is routinely larger than that of CS (more than three times larger, on average).

why_this_data.value: Resolve disk from envelope and outflow at ~0.3'' angular resolution; Band 6 covers many lines

evidence.quote: This goal requires us to resolve structures of a few hundred au, which translates, at the distance of Taurus, into an angular resolution on the order of 0.3$''$.

limitations_admitted.value: Moderate resolution and symmetry assumption limit z/r accuracy; optical thinness uncertain

evidence.quote: We however caution that the moderate angular resolution, the small size of the rings (in particular in Haro 6-13), and the assumption of azimuthally symmetric structures (cite: Podio2019) limit the accuracy of our constraints.

referee_caveats_inferred: Column densities rely on optically thin LTE with a wide assumed temperature range, giving factor-of-several ranges
Visual fitting of z/r has no formal uncertainties
Heterogeneous resolution and recoverable scale between Cycle 4 and Cycle 6 data complicate comparisons
Continuum over-subtraction and absorption affect inner-disk results
